_comment: wp_container — passive PUBLIC container-registry OSINT (Docker Hub, GHCR, Quay, any OCI v2 registry for a single image). Endpoint templates, size caps, the member-path patterns read out of layer tarballs, and the secret SHAPES matched against config blobs / history / layer files live here (RULE 3) so a registry API change or a new key shape is a data edit. Everything here is public vendor vocabulary or a regex — never a case value, never a credential. Placeholders `{ns}`, `{repo}`, `{owner}`, `{img}`, `{ref}`, `{digest}`, `{page}`, `{page_size}` are URL-safe values substituted by the caller.

settings._comment: timeout_seconds = per-request socket timeout (wp_common floors it at the engine CALL_TIMEOUT). page_size / max_repos bound the namespace listing walk. max_images = how many of a namespace's repositories get their config blob inspected (0 = list only); max_tags = tags returned per repository. platform = the os/arch picked out of a multi-arch index. config_max_bytes caps a config blob read. layer_max_bytes / layers_total_max_bytes cap layer streaming (only with --layers): a layer larger than the cap is read PARTIALLY (members before the cap are still scanned) and flagged truncated; once the total is reached no further layer is opened. member_max_bytes caps one tar member read; max_members_per_layer caps how many tar headers are walked per layer; max_history_cmds caps history lines returned per image.

registries._comment: Per-registry endpoints. `aliases` = hostnames a ref may be written with. `registry` = the OCI distribution base. `token` = the anonymous pull-token template (avoids the 401 round trip; when absent or failing the module follows the WWW-Authenticate Bearer challenge instead). Listing endpoints are registry-specific and keyless: Docker Hub v2 namespaces API + the user/org profile — Hub refuses anonymous paging past ~100 items (403 'pagination offset too large'), so `orderings` are walked in turn and the names unioned; Quay public repository API; GHCR has NO keyless listing API, so the owner's public GitHub packages page is read for container package names (`ghcr_pages`, tried in order).

media_types._comment: Accept header for manifest GETs (index/list first so a multi-arch tag resolves to its index, then the platform entry is fetched by digest), and the media types recognised as an index vs a single manifest. Layer media types containing `zstd` need the optional stdlib compression.zstd (Python 3.14+); otherwise that layer is skipped with a note.

identity_labels._comment: Image LABEL keys read as identity LEADS (rung lead, never an edge — a namespace or label is often a personal dev/contractor account or a copied base-image label). `source` labels yield source_repo_url.

member_paths._comment: Regexes (Python re, case-insensitive) on a layer tar member path: a member is READ and secret-scanned only if it matches `include` and no `exclude`. Excludes drop language runtimes / vendored packages / CA bundles whose YAML/JSON/PEM files are public and drown the signal.

secret_patterns._comment: Secret SHAPES (Python re). `group` = which capture group is the secret value (0 = whole match). The first five mirror the credential shapes scripts/audit.sh 5b blocks from the tracked tree; the rest are common vendor/structure shapes. `named_assignment` is the generic KEY=value catch for a secret-NAMED key; its value is dropped when it matches `placeholder_values`.

secret_env_name._comment: An Env / build-arg NAME matching `regex` with a non-placeholder value of >= min_len chars is reported as kind env_named_secret even when no vendor shape matches. `benign` names are never reported (base-image version pins and checksums).

placeholder_values._comment: Values that are templates, not secrets (case-insensitive regex, matched against the whole value).

caveats._comment: Fixed caveat strings attached to output (RULE 5).
caveats.identity: LEAD only: a registry namespace or image label is often a personal developer / contractor / CI account or a label copied from a base image — corroborate before naming anyone; never an edge on this signal alone.
caveats.secret: FACT that a credential-shaped string is published in a public image; not attribution and NOT validated. Values are never printed — preview is first/last 3 chars, sha256 identifies the value for dedupe.
